note: Adapted from the species description of Alyscotermes trestus in Sands (1972), originally in English: the species lacks soldiers and only the alate and the worker are described; measurement-table headers, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and figures damaged by OCR in the measurement tables are omitted; the remaining characters covered by the generic diagnosis are not repeated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The diagnostic characters have been discussed in comparison with A. kilimandjaricus. The enteric valve appendages of the worker are asymmetrically developed and may represent an early stage in the evolution of an Anaorotermes-type valve; the abdomen of the worker shows signs of splitting in some specimens.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellow, pilosity sparse, scattered, orange. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27, Pcl/Ri 2.37. On the left mandible the accessory marginal tooth is larger and more prominent than the third marginal tooth, separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a broad, deep notch, composite ratio 6.42; on the right mandible the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is slightly longer than that of the second marginal tooth, composite ratio 10.13. The enteric valve appendages bear 7–12 prominent spines at positions 3 and 4, set on slightly sclerotized cushions, together with numerous small spines and spinules; positions 1 and 2 bear 1–3 prominent spines, the cushions unsclerotized, with additional small spines and spinules. The membranous wall of the valve bears minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark chestnut brown, very dark above the ocelli; fontanelle elliptical, flat, slightly raised or depressed in the middle, surface slightly rough, slightly smaller than the ocellus, chestnut brown; median spot circular or briefly elliptical, faint, slightly concave, chestnut brown, semicircular; antennae dark brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum chestnut brown, transverse sutures distinct; femora dark brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellowish brown. Abdominal tergites and dorsolateral spiracles chestnut brown, sternites and ventrolateral spiracles brown, the middle of the sternites yellowish brown; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule unevenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli small, separated from the compound eye by their own least diameter or slightly more; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.22–0.25, posterior margin broad and evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Cephalic pilosity brown, coarsely felted, concealed by numerous unevenly projecting setae.
